title: Derived sections and Hom along affine etale limits
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, let $A$ be a finite field, and use ordinary small-etale and small-pro-etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be a small cofiltered system of affine etale finitely presented $X$-schemes with affine transition maps, put $U=\varprojlim_iU_i$, and let $j_i:U_i\to X$ and $j:U\to X$ be the structure maps [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra, def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. For $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], the canonical pullback maps give natural isomorphisms of complexes of $A$-modules
$$\varinjlim_i R\Gamma((U_i)_{\mathrm{et}},j_i^*L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{proet}},(\nu_X^*L)|_U),$$
$$\varinjlim_i R\operatorname{Hom}_{(U_i)_{\mathrm{et}},A}(j_i^*K,j_i^*L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_{U_{\mathrm{et}},A}(j^*K,j^*L).$$
Here $\nu_X$ is the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], restriction on the first line is to the pro-etale slice over $U$, filtered colimits are derived filtered colimits (equivalently exact filtered colimits of complexes), and $R\operatorname{Hom}$ is global derived Hom, with $H^n$ equal to $\operatorname{Hom}(K,L[n])$. Both comparisons are induced by restriction of sections and morphisms and agree with evaluation. Only a lower bound on $L$ is needed; a cohomological-dimension bound for $X$ or $U_i$ is not required.

source.place: Lemmas 6.3.14 and the affine-limit computation in the proof of 6.3.16; bounded-below comparison of Section 5.1; for fields Remark 6.3.2 identifies constructibility conventions

proof.text: Apply [det-sf-comparison-affine-continuity] to the given presentation and $L$: its equivalence of filtered derived section complexes is exactly the first displayed comparison, with the same restriction maps and the pro-etale slice interpretation. Its hypotheses are precisely affineness of the stages, cofiltered smallness, affine transitions, discrete coefficients, and bounded-below $L$. This already proves the sections assertion, without a dimension bound.

For the Hom assertion, apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal] to $I^{\mathrm{op}}$ and take opposites on the scheme diagram. It preserves its limit and all the filtered colimits in question. We may thus assume a nonempty directed index set. Fix a stage $0$ and restrict to $i\geq0$: a representative at $i$ moves to any common upper bound of $i,0$, and equality of two representatives is still witnessed at a common later stage. The same common-upper-bound construction extends cones uniquely, so this tail also preserves the limit. Put $S=U_0$, $L_0=j_0^*L$, $K_0=j_0^*K$, and denote later and limit pullbacks by subscripts $i$ and $U$. The functor of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] preserves cohomology and lower bounds, and its derived functor preserves triangles [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. The cohomology sheaves of $K_0$ are $h^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)$, $h=j_0$, so $K_0$ is bounded in the same range; we check each is constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Take a stratification $(\iota_k:Z_k\to X)$ witnessing constructibility of $\mathcal H^q(K)$. The base changes $\iota'_k:Z'_k=Z_k\times_XS\to S$ form a stratification with strata $h^{-1}(X_k)$ [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification], which are constructible subsets [lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage]. With $g_k:Z'_k\to Z_k$ the projection, $\iota_k'^{-1}h^{-1}\cong g_k^{-1}\iota_k^{-1}$, both being inverse image along $\iota_kg_k=h\iota'_k$. If $\{W_m\to Z_k\}$ is an etale covering with $(\iota_k^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K))|_{W_m}\cong\underline{M_m}$, $M_m$ finite, its base change to $Z'_k$ is an etale covering on whose members the pullback is $\cong\underline{M_m}$ [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant]. Fix $b$ with $L_0\in D^{\geq b}$; every $L_i,L_U$ has this same bound.

source.place: Tags 0032 (directed cofinal replacement), 03Q1 (inverse image), 03RZ (constructibility); elementary tail argument written here

proof.text: For any scheme $T$ and etale object $v:V\to T$, put $P_V=v_!A_V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian], this is the sheafification of the free module presheaf $A_T[h_V]$, with coefficients in the constant ring sheaf $A_T$. The adjunction of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] and [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] give $\operatorname{Hom}(P_V,M)=M(V)$: the map sends $f$ to $f(e_{1_V})$, with inverse sending $e_\varphi$ to the restriction of that section along $\varphi$. Choose a bounded-below injective representative $J$ of any $N\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ by [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution]. By [lem-pe-injective-complex-slice-section-model], $J(V)$ computes $R\Gamma(V,N|_V)$ and its restriction maps. Apply the preceding ordinary Hom formula degree by degree. By [lem-sc-kinjective-quasi-iso-comparison], cohomology of $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(P_V,J)$ computes $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)}(P_V,N[n])$: cocycles are maps $P_V\to J[n]$, and boundaries are null homotopies. We obtain the natural identification with $H^nR\Gamma(V,N|_V)$ for every integer $n$.

source.place: Tag 03DI, equation-map-lower-shriek-OU-into-module; bounded-injective evaluation on localized sites

proof.text: Define $\theta_C^n:\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}(C_i,L_i[n])\to\operatorname{Hom}(C_U,L_U[n])$ by inverse image, for $C\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. For an affine etale $V\to S$ take $C=P_V$. The sheaf base-change isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules], together with pullback of constants [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant], identifies $C_i$ with $P_{V_i}$ for $V_i=V\times_SU_i$, and likewise at $U$. All $V_i$ are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], hence qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Their transitions are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-transition], applied to the identity on $V,S$ and $U_{i'}\to U_i$. The universal property of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $V_U$ with $\varprojlim_iV_i$: a map to either side is a map to $V$ and a compatible cone to $U_i$ agreeing over $S$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-continuity] to the pullbacks of $L_0|_V$ on this system (with initial stage $V$). Step 3 identifies its restriction comparison in degree $n$ with $\theta_{P_V}^n$. Thus this map is an isomorphism for every $n$. The identification is of the actual map: pulling back $e_\varphi\mapsto s|_\varphi$ gives $e_{\varphi'}\mapsto (s|_{V_i})|_{\varphi'}$ on the fibre product, which is the section restriction formula.

Let $\mathcal E$ consist of the $C$ for which all $\theta_C^n$ are isomorphisms. It contains the generators of step 4 and their finite sums and shifts. It is closed under taking the third object of a triangle when it contains the other two. Indeed inverse image gives triangles and their commuting comparison ladders [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact], and its rotations and shifts, to get the two long exact Hom sequences. Their filtered colimit remains exact by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact]. The five consecutive terms around any degree have four comparison isomorphisms, so [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] gives the fifth. In particular every finite complex with terms finite sums of the generators belongs to $\mathcal E$: induct on its number of nonzero terms using its brutal filtration. Adding its lowest term expresses it as a cone of the differential to the already constructed higher-degree subcomplex (with the appropriate shift). These are the cone triangles defining the derived triangulation [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 0149 (lemma-representable-homological), Tag 05RR (derived cone triangulation); finite brutal-filtration induction

proof.text: Let $F$ be a constructible sheaf on the affine scheme $S$. For a positive integer $r$, use the exact sequence provided by [lem-trf-constructible-etale-finite-affine-syzygy]: $0\to K_r\to E_{r-1}\to\cdots\to E_0\to F\to0$, each $E_a$ a finite sum of affine etale generators. Form the finite complex $P_r=(E_{r-1}\to\cdots\to E_0)$ in degrees $1-r,\ldots,0$ and its augmentation $P_r\to F[0]$. The cone $C_r$ has $K_r$ as its sole cohomology, in degree $-r$: this follows directly by computing the kernels and images in the displayed exact sequence. Thus $C_r\in D^{\leq-r}$, and $P_r\in\mathcal E$ by step 5. Exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] preserves this sequence, the cone calculation, and the bound $C_{r,i},C_{r,U}\in D^{\leq-r}$. No infinite resolution or projectivity of $E_a$ is being assumed.

source.place: Tags 095N (finite affine presentations), 03RZ (constructible kernels), 03S8 (constructible generators); finite cone computation

proof.text: Fix $n\in\mathbf Z$ and choose $r\geq1$ with $r>n+1-b$. The bounds of step 6 and standard t-structure orthogonality [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category, def-weil-t-structure] imply $\operatorname{Hom}(C_{r,i},L_i[n])=\operatorname{Hom}(C_{r,i},L_i[n+1])=0$, and the same at $U$: indeed $-r<b-n-1\leq b-n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact] to $P_{r,i}\to F_i\to C_{r,i}\to P_{r,i}[1]$. The exact segment with those two zero end terms gives $\operatorname{Hom}(F_i,L_i[n])\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(P_{r,i},L_i[n])$, and similarly on $U$. These are precomposition by the pulled-back augmentation; they therefore commute with further pullback. Their colimits identify $\theta_F^n$ with $\theta_{P_r}^n$, already an isomorphism by step 5. Since $n$ was arbitrary, every constructible sheaf $F$ lies in $\mathcal E$. The choice of $r$ depends on $n,b$, not on $i$ and not on a cohomological-dimension bound.

source.place: Standard derived t-structure orthogonality and Tag 0149; finite-resolution cutoff argument written here

proof.text: Apply finite Postnikov induction to the bounded constructible complex $K_0$. The successive triangles of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] are $\tau_{\leq q-1}K_0\to\tau_{\leq q}K_0\to\mathcal H^q(K_0)[-q]\to\tau_{\leq q-1}K_0[1]$. Each shifted cohomology sheaf belongs to $\mathcal E$ by step 7 and shift closure. Below the lowest nonzero cohomology the truncation is zero; induction up to the highest degree, using triangle closure from step 5, proves $K_0\in\mathcal E$. Consequently the second displayed comparison is an isomorphism on every cohomology group.

source.place: Tag 08J5, canonical truncation triangles; finite Postnikov induction

proof.text: Finally, the group comparisons just proved are the cohomology of the specified comparison of global derived Hom complexes: [lem-sfb-derived-internal-hom-sections-model] computes global derived Hom by the ordinary Hom complex into a K-injective representative and identifies its $H^n$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(K,L[n])$. The representative relations for a filtered module colimit are those of the underlying group colimit, with scalar multiplication induced on representatives. Exactness of filtered group colimits [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact] and [src-weil-homology-preserves-exact-colimits] therefore identify cohomology of the filtered Hom-complex colimit with the colimit of these groups. A map inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology is inverted in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All maps used are inverse-image maps on morphisms or restrictions on sections, so the comparisons are natural in both variables. More explicitly, for a derived morphism $f:C\to L[n]$ and a pullback $h^*$ the map used is $f\mapsto h^*f$; for a section $s$ it is $s\mapsto s|$. Evaluation commutes with these maps because $h^*(f\circ a)=h^*f\circ h^*a$, and in the free models its formula is the basis-element calculation in steps 3-4. Homotopies, being equations $f-g=dh+hd$, obey the same restriction identity. Hence these are the evaluation-compatible canonical comparisons, independent of resolution choices.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (derived internal Hom), Tag 03DI (evaluation), exact filtered-colimit cohomology; canonical pullback compatibility
